title: Minimum Wage Brisbane: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the minimum wage in Brisbane. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,270.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Brisbane for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The national minimum wage applies in Brisbane as elsewhere. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual workers receive at least $33.05 per hour including the 25% casual loading. Some awards or enterprise agreements may set higher rates.

faqs.q: How much tax and Medicare levy will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The estimate here uses the full tax-free threshold and single Medicare reduction thresholds from 2025–26.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**

For a full-time employee, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Employment Standards. This is the most common benchmark for full-time work in Australia. If you work different hours, adjust the formula accordingly.

Knowing your annual pay also lets you estimate your fortnightly income. Simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,000, your fortnightly pay is $2,000 before tax and super.

## Minimum Wage in Brisbane: What You Need to Know

The national minimum wage applies to all employees in Australia, including those in Brisbane. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual workers receive a minimum of $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% casual loading.

It is important to note that the national minimum wage is a floor. Many employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher pay rates. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Retail Award may have different minimums for specific roles. Always check your award or agreement with the Fair Work Ombudsman.

The term "minimum wage brisbane" often refers to the national rate, as there is no separate Brisbane minimum. However, some local government or state awards may apply to certain public sector roles. For most private sector workers, the national minimum wage is the starting point.

### Casual Loading and Award Rates

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. When using the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) tool, you should enter your base rate (without loading) and then select the casual loading checkbox. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Award rates often include built-in loadings or penalties for weekend or shift work. The national minimum wage is separate from award rates. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay may be higher than the national minimum.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate the tax you will owe. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. Low-income earners may be eligible for a reduction. The estimates here use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation.

For example, if your annual gross pay is $52,270 (the minimum wage for 38 hours), your estimated tax would be calculated on the amount above $18,200. After the Medicare levy, your take-home pay would be lower. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual salary is $52,270, your employer would contribute an additional $6,272.40 to your super fund.

Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. When comparing a salary offer, remember that the total cost to the employer includes super. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice and other arrangements can affect your take-home pay.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Calculation

The [the timesheet](/), our home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. You can also check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The tool uses the standard 38-hour week but you can adjust the hours if needed.

For a quick reference, the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains the formula in more detail. The [reference tables](/data) provide pre-calculated figures for common rates.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on your hourly rate multiplied by hours per week and 52 weeks. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Average Pay Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians, and may not reflect the pay for your specific job. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more details.

Remember that the national minimum wage is a floor, not a target. Many workers earn above it. If you are negotiating a salary, use the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources to research typical rates for your occupation and location.
